dossier.public_summary: The claimed 13.1-day dip varies wildly in depth from almost undetectable to much deeper within the same instrument, with most of the signal coming from a couple of unusually deep events. That depth instability, paired with strong starspot variability, is a sign of stellar activity or a blended variable rather than a transiting planet, so it is rejected as a planet candidate.

reasons.why: Depth changes by ~3.7x across sectors (536 ppm in sector 42 to 7376 ppm in sector 44) is not a planet and rules out a stable on-target transit at this period.
Variation is real within the same pipeline, not a calibration offset between products, so different apertures/pointing are not the cause.
reasons.value: changes_within_a_source, p_constant_all 7.329e-26, SPOC 2-min p_constant 1.06e-16, TESS-SPOC p_constant 1.96e-07

reasons.why: Individual transits are inconsistent; the signal is dominated by a few deep outliers, inconsistent with a planet's fixed depth.

reasons.why: The dip period is ~2.46x the measured spotted rotation and phase_curve amplitude_ppm 402.9 with variability_chi2_dof 2.324 shows large spot modulation, supporting stellar variability/spots or a close binary over a planet despite flat shape v_sigma -3.868.
